items.sentence: The NHS describes sumatriptan as available as tablets, a nasal spray and an injection.
items.note: NHS side-effects page mentions injection-site and nasal spray reactions; tablets from NHS sumatriptan page

items.sentence: The NHS says most adults can take sumatriptan, that it is not officially approved for children, and that a specialist doctor may sometimes prescribe it for a child.
items.note: search summary of NHS who-can page: most adults up to 65; not approved for children, specialist may prescribe

items.sentence: Sumatriptan is a triptan, a type of medicine that acts on serotonin (5-HT1) receptors.
items.note: search summary: triptan, serotonin 5-HT1 receptor agonist; page attribution uncertain

items.sentence: It is taken once a headache has started, not to prevent attacks.
items.note: NHS: relieves symptoms but does not prevent

items.sentence: Because triptans act on serotonin, taking them with some antidepressants or St John's wort can raise the risk of serotonin syndrome, a severe side effect.
Feeling sick and dizziness are the side effects the NHS lists most often.
Flushing and tiredness are also listed.
Reactions where the injection is given or with the nasal spray can occur.
Most people have no side effects or only minor ones, and serious reactions are rare.
The NHS lists high blood pressure as a reason sumatriptan may not be suitable, although it may be possible if blood pressure is now well controlled by treatment.
The NHS says sumatriptan is not taken with ergotamine or other triptans, because this raises the risk of side effects.
The NHS says sumatriptan can be used in pregnancy if needed, with the doctor weighing risks and benefits.
The NHS advises against driving, cycling or using machinery until dizziness or tiredness from sumatriptan has passed.
The NHS lists a severe allergic reaction and symptoms of a heart attack as possible serious reactions that need a 999 call, and says to call NHS 111 for other serious side effects.
A Scottish NHS primary-care guideline recommends limiting how often triptans are used, because frequent use of acute migraine treatment can itself cause headaches.
items.note: search summary of Scottish guideline (medication overuse headache)
